source.title: APP: Anytime Progressive Pruning
source.authors: Diganta Misra; Bharat Runwal; Tian-Long Chen; Zhang-Yang Wang; I. Rish

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports non-monotonic generalization-gap curves and compares them to cited double-descent work, but it does not measure test error over model size, epochs, or sample size as the claim versions require.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Deep Double Descent and reports its own generalization-gap curves. Generalization gap is not the test error named in the versions, so these results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version, not as tests of a version. Curve values are not reported numerically in the text.
record.test_reason: The paper only likens its own generalization-gap curves to Nakkiran et al. Those curves track train-minus-validation accuracy over training iterations, under progressive pruning and replay-growing data. It never sweeps model size, epochs or sample count to measure test error around an interpolation threshold.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that APP substantially lowers the generalization gap versus the dense baseline and one-shot pruning. They report non-monotonic gap transitions in high-megabatch ALMA and leave the cause as an open question.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines progressive pruning in ALMA and reports test accuracy, cumulative error rate, and generalization gap; it does not sweep model size, epochs, or sample size to measure double descent in test error.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported generalization-gap behavior varies with the number of megabatches and pruning method; APP's gap oscillates in the critical regime, and APP remains relatively stable at |SB| = 25 while baseline and Anytime OSP rise toward the end.

fits_no_version.finding: Under long-sequence ALMA (|SB| = 50, 100) on CIFAR-10 with ResNet-50, the generalization gap over iterations goes from underfitting, to sharp overfitting, to gradual decline. At |SB| = 25 the gap rises late for the baseline and Anytime OSP but stays stable for APP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In sequential megabatch training with replay, the train-validation accuracy gap can change non-monotonically over iterations, depending on the number of megabatches and the pruning method.

fits_no_version.finding: The same non-monotonic gap transition appears in the few-shot Restricted ImageNet runs with |SB| = 30 and 70. APP shows a lower gap in all plotted subplots.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization-gap trajectories in few-shot ALMA can be non-monotonic, and progressive pruning lowers the gap.

record.problems: For findings relevant here, the paper gives generalization-gap curves rather than test-error results for the claimed axes. The relevant curve values are presented in figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The authors state that the reason for the observed transitions remains unresolved.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep of test error; the pruned versus dense sizes (8.6 M vs 23.5 M) are method comparisons, not a capacity sweep.
Test error over epochs is not plotted. The generalization gap over iterations (Fig. 8, 9) rises then falls, which is not a fall-rise-fall test-error curve.
Per-megabatch test error as data accumulates (Fig. 4) is not examined near an interpolation threshold, and no peak is reported.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No label-noise or regularization sweep of a test-error peak. The single weight-decay ablation reports only final metrics.
No alternative parameter count is used.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are correctly linked to none. Their states describe the gap-curve shape, not any version. The gap curves are confounded: the training set grows with replay and sparsity increases at each megabatch, so even shape-wise they are not an epoch-wise double-descent test. No numeric curve values are given; all evidence is figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep of model size measuring test error around an interpolation threshold.
The paper plots generalization gap over training iterations, not test error over epochs.
No increase in training sample count near an interpolation threshold is tested for its effect on test error.
No capacity sweep across model classes measures risk around an interpolation point.
No single effective-complexity measure is evaluated as a predictor of peak location.
The paper does not test label-noise or regularization dependence of a test-error peak, multiple descent peaks, or disappearance under optimal regularization.
No alternative parameter-count measure is used to assess whether a second descent becomes U-shaped.
